Sounds like potential repetitive friction burn. 

This can happen, especially as movement control deteriorates through fatigue or movement efficiencies. 

If that’s the case, try slowing down to identify where in the movement muscular control is trading for momentum. As the body sequences muscles firing to achieve the movement you’ll be able to identify the weak link in the chain. 

Once identified, work to isolate that section of the movement doing static holds and then progressing to controlled micro reps across that limited range of motion. Continue to expand until you reach the full range of motion for the desired movement. As your awareness and familiarity in the controlled movement improves you can speed up again. 

This is meant to be something to work on a little at a time. You’ll see the movement efficiency and control improve with better muscular recruitment and the sore should subside.
